Score a reading recipe's answer against acceptable answers

Source: R/doc-bench-qa.R
gr_scorer_answer.Rd

An hr_scorer() for the gr_answers that gr_arm() returns, against a reference from gr_qa_reference(). An answer is right when its text contains any of the item's acceptable answers, after both are folded the same way: lower case, runs of white space as one space, and thousands separators dropped between digits, so "1,204", "1 204" (with a no-break or thin space) and "1204" are the same. A number in a label is written in plain digits, so the label 100000 accepts "100,000". A number is matched whole: "45.2" is not found in "145.2" or "45.25", and "12" is not found in ".12" (the decimal 0.12) or in "-12". A unit written against a number does not hide it ("45.2m" and "5mg" contain "45.2" and "5"), and a hyphen between two numbers is a range, not a minus sign ("12-15" contains "15"). On an unanswerable item, labelled "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT", the answer is right when is_not_found() says it reports the document does not hold the answer.

Usage

gr_scorer_answer()

Value

An hr_scorer() named "answer_contains".

Details

An answer that is not right gets the first of these failure kinds that applies:

"parse_failure"

There is no answer text: the output is not a string or has no answer or text, or the text is blank.

"budget_stop"

The answer is partial and notes that a limit stopped it: the spending limit (cost_cap_reached), the call limit (call_cap_reached), or another limit that refused a request (limit_refused).

"refusal"

A model refused a request of the run: a step of the answer's trace finished with reason "refusal" or "content_filter", or the output is a refused gr_result.

"not_in_document"

An answer was expected and the reader said the document does not hold one.

"wrong"

Anything else, an answer to an unanswerable question included.

An output that carries its own failure_kind keeps it, and a failed gr_result is an "error", as with hr_scorer_exact(). A stopped or refused run that still found an acceptable answer is right. A not-found answer from a run that was stopped or refused is that stop on an unanswerable item as well: a reader that ran out of budget did not look.

The outcome is the answer's folded text.

See also

gr_qa_reference(), gr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_scorer()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

s <- gr_scorer_answer()
item <- list(question = "How many units?", document = gr_example())
s$fn(item, "Sheffield produced 12,400 units.", "12400")$correct
#> [1] TRUE
s$fn(item, "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT", "12400")$failure_kind
#> [1] "not_in_document"
s$fn(item, "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT", "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT")$correct
#> [1] TRUE
